newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lebanon said to swoop on Christians.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon said to swoop on Christians.

text.p: Dozens of Christians have been detained in Lebanon following an attack on Syrian workers in the country, the Paris office of exiled Lebanese former general Michel Aoun said on Friday.
A spokeswoman for Aoun said she could not give a precise number of arrests, but they seemed to run into several dozens.

Aoun's Rally for Lebanon movement said detentions continued on Friday, and it had requested an emergency meeting with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette to urge him to intervene and help end the swoops.
It said Charles Rustom, a senior official of the National Liberal Party, a rightwing Christian group, and Charbel Charmi, the bodyguard of the party's leader Dory Chamoun, were among those detained.
The spokeswoman said Rustom had been held at his home but now appeared to be free.
Gunmen in a speeding car opened fire at a small van carrying three Syrian civilians on Wednesday in the Christian area of Tabarja, 28 km (18 miles) north of Beirut, killing one and wounding another.
No-one has claimed responsibility for the attack.

An explosion on the same day near a Syrian army intelligence centre in the northern Lebanese city of Tripoli was at first reported to be a bomb but Lebanon's National News Agency later said a detonator accidentally exploded in burning garbage without causing damage or injuries.

Aoun was forced into exile in 1990 after heading the Christian-led Lebanese army in an unsuccessful and bloody effort to oust Syrian forces from the country. Damascus is Beirut's main power broker with some 35,000 troops in Lebanon.
